**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning negative. In 2024 AMLO did not look like a ruler who was fully open to independent accountability: the clearest evidence points to pressure on media, transparency bodies, and courts. There is some counterevidence in the form of ongoing Ayotzinapa handling, public anti-corruption enforcement against connected business actors, and a few procedural concessions, but these are narrower than the negative pattern.

- [Mexico](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) - Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, 2024-06-17. The overview says AMLO’s final year included repeated attacks on journalists and a doxxing-style episode where he displayed a reporter’s phone number on broadcast; that is direct evidence of intimidation rather than protection of independent scrutiny. `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.2`

- [Mexico: Proposed Constitutional Changes Threaten Rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-08-30. HRW warned that the reform package would weaken judicial independence, expand military power, and erode privacy/transparency safeguards, which would make it harder to expose concealed wrongdoing or use courts and watchdogs against the executive. `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`

- [Mexico](https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024) - Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House reported a covert SEDENA cyberspace unit that monitored critics and used inauthentic accounts, alongside broader surveillance with little oversight; this is strong evidence of state power being used to chill investigation and punish critics. `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.2`

- [Mexico's Planned Judicial Reform Is Major Risk To Democracy, Says U.S. Ambassador](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-planned-judicial-reform-is-major-risk-to-democracy-says-us-ambassador-3584038) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-08-22. The U.S. ambassador said the judicial reform threatened democracy and the trade relationship; as evidence for this lens, it supports the claim that AMLO was moving to neutralize a countervailing institution rather than tolerate review of his government. `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`

- [Mexico's sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-09-15. Reuters reported the overhaul was enacted amid criticism that it weakened judicial independence and investor confidence; that is direct evidence of neutralizing courts that could restrain executive misconduct or self-dealing. `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`

- [AMLO's government publicly presented the Totalplay tax-evasion case](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/gobierno-federal-presenta-caso-de-evasion-fiscal-de-totalplay-debe-mas-de-mil-500-millones-de-pesos-al-sat/) - Presidencia de México, 2024-03-15. This is counterevidence: the administration publicized and pursued a tax-evasion case against a politically connected firm, which cuts against a blanket claim that AMLO used state power only to protect allies. `7B.7`, `7B.4`, `7B.6`

- [Segob report to Ayotzinapa families](https://www.gob.mx/segob/prensa/presidente-amlo-entregara-informe-a-madres-y-padres-ayotzinapa-con-anexos-que-sustentan-cada-respuesta-370094) - Secretaría de Gobernación, 2024-07-03. The government said it had searched 251 sites and was still working the case with the families; this is limited positive evidence that AMLO did not simply shut down or hide an emblematic abuse investigation. `7B.7`, `7B.6`

- [Versión estenográfica, 24 June 2024](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/articulos/version-estenografica-conferencia-de-prensa-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador-del-24-de-junio-de-2024) - Presidencia de México, 2024-06-24. AMLO said he had no proof the Army was responsible for Ayotzinapa, but that if proof appeared “se actúa,” and that he had not exonerated anyone; this is weak but real counterevidence to a full concealment narrative. `7B.7`, `7B.6`

- [AMLO reveals journalist’s phone number](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/mexicos-president-defends-decision-share-174417727.html) - Reuters via Yahoo News Canada, 2024-02-26. AMLO publicly displayed a New York Times journalist’s phone number and defended the move; that is direct intimidation of a truth-teller and fits the “punish investigators / media” part of the lens. `7B.7`, `7B.6`, `7B.2`

- [AMLO’s own comments on anti-corruption and investigative cases](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/gobierno-de-mexico-mantiene-demanda-en-florida-para-recuperar-634-mdd-por-trama-de-corrupcion-de-garcia-luna/) - Presidencia de México, 2024-02-16. The administration kept asset-recovery litigation alive in a major corruption case, which is modest counterevidence against a pure concealment/self-protection story. `7B.7`, `7B.4`, `7B.6`

**Search Gap**  
I did not find strong 2024 evidence that AMLO personally ordered concealment of his own assets or a single documented “smoking gun” of direct obstruction. The record is stronger on pattern evidence: weakening courts and transparency institutions, intimidation of journalists, and surveillance/pressure on critics.
